episode.title: Resolve read-only path patterns against the repository root
episode.before: At first parent 9edf9b4186ea08e2fb98897697e4f9b62836bb6f, the read-only command expanded every input with glob.glob(expanded_pattern, recursive=True), so relative pattern discovery used the process current working directory. The discovered path was subsequently passed to coder.abs_root_path(), which joins relative paths to coder.root. After the process changed into a repository subdirectory, a repository-root-relative input such as subdir/test_read_only_file.txt was searched beneath that subdirectory and produced no match, even though later path normalization treated the same input as repository-root-relative.
episode.after: At b911ceaa6125bbb8e11fe741dab10bbf9731bf12, the read-only command calls glob.glob(expanded_pattern, recursive=True, root_dir=self.coder.root). Relative patterns are therefore discovered from the same repository-root base used by coder.abs_root_path(), independent of the process current working directory. Absolute and tilde-expanded inputs remain supported. A regression test changes into a repository subdirectory, adds a file using its repository-root-relative name, confirms that its absolute path enters the read-only set, drops it using the same name, and confirms removal.
episode.diff: The merge changes one implementation line in aider/commands.py by supplying coder.root as glob's root_dir, aligning relative-pattern discovery with downstream repository-root path resolution. It adds a 37-line regression test in tests/basic/test_commands.py covering the non-root-working-directory scenario and the add/drop lifecycle. The focused test could not be executed in the available environment because the system Python lacked pytest and the discovered pytest environment lacked GitPython; git diff --check reported no patch whitespace errors.

evidence_units.claim: The pinned merge commit is b911ceaa6125bbb8e11fe741dab10bbf9731bf12, has first parent 9edf9b4186ea08e2fb98897697e4f9b62836bb6f and second parent ba9fdaa755c82994d7aff7404d689d6c721ab283, and identifies PR 2126 as fixing an inability to use the read-only command from another working directory.
In the first parent, cmd_read_only expands user input and invokes glob.glob(expanded_pattern, recursive=True), leaving relative-pattern lookup dependent on the process current working directory.
The implementation adds root_dir=self.coder.root to the glob invocation and makes no other production-code change in the first-parent diff.
After globbing, cmd_read_only passes each returned path to coder.abs_root_path before checking whether it is a file or directory and adding it to the read-only collection.
coder.abs_root_path constructs Path(self.root) / path and converts it to a safe absolute path, establishing the repository root as the downstream base for relative paths.

The added regression test creates a file under a repository subdirectory, changes the process current directory into that subdirectory, invokes cmd_read_only with a repository-root-relative path, and asserts by os.path.samefile that the file is present in coder.abs_read_only_fnames.
The same regression test invokes cmd_drop with the repository-root-relative name and asserts that the file is no longer present in coder.abs_read_only_fnames.

An adjacent pre-existing test supplies an absolute temporary-file path to cmd_read_only and verifies that the external file is added, providing coverage for the absolute-path behavior that the root-base correction must preserve.

The focused regression test was not runnable in the available environments: /usr/bin/python3 had no pytest module, while /home/chenyujia/tritonToLlvm/.venv_triton_ascend_probe/bin/pytest failed test collection because the git module was absent.
evidence_units.source: Attempted python3 -m pytest and /home/chenyujia/tritonToLlvm/.venv_triton_ascend_probe/bin/pytest for tests/basic/test_commands.py::TestCommands::test_cmd_read_only_from_working_dir on archived parent and pinned revisions

evidence_units.claim: The first-parent patch passes git diff --check for the two changed files.
evidence_units.source: git diff --check b911ceaa^1 b911ceaa -- aider/commands.py tests/basic/test_commands.py

evidence_units.claim: The regression test added by the pinned commit is absent from the first parent and contributes the entire 37-line test-file addition.

candidate_atomics.name: align-relative-pattern-resolution-base
candidate_atomics.title: Align relative pattern discovery with the authoritative resource root
candidate_atomics.description: Bind relative pattern expansion to the same authoritative root used by downstream path normalization so a process working-directory change cannot redirect or invalidate resource selection, while preserving absolute-path handling.

semantic_action.intent: Make read-only resource selection consistent and independent of the process current working directory.
semantic_action.module_role: Command-layer resource selector that discovers user-supplied paths before registering them under a non-editable access policy.
semantic_action.pre_state: Relative input patterns are discovered against the process current working directory, but returned paths are normalized against the command session's repository root; the two bases can diverge after a working-directory change.
semantic_action.post_state: Relative input patterns are discovered and normalized against the same repository root, while absolute or user-expanded paths remain eligible for discovery.
semantic_action.validation: Change into a nested repository directory, select an existing file by its repository-root-relative path, and verify its canonical absolute path enters the read-only set; retain the absolute external-file test as a compatibility oracle.

candidate_workflows.name: enforce-stable-root-relative-resource-selection
candidate_workflows.title: Keep policy-scoped file selection stable across working-directory changes
candidate_workflows.description: Repair a command whose resource-discovery base differs from its canonicalization base by establishing one authoritative root, applying it during relative-pattern expansion, and validating both the failing nested-directory case and preserved absolute-path behavior.

workflow_graph.goal: Ensure that files named relative to the repository root can be added to and removed from a read-only policy set regardless of the process current working directory.
when_to_use: A command accepts relative paths or glob patterns for policy-scoped resources and fails or resolves inconsistently after the process changes into a nested directory.
Path discovery and later canonicalization use different implicit bases, allowing ambient working-directory state to affect which resource receives the policy.
anti_goals: Do not broaden editable access or convert read-only resources into editable resources.
Do not restrict already-supported absolute or user-home-expanded resource paths.
Do not change repository membership rules, file contents, or the process current working directory as the repair.
not_applicable_when: The command contract intentionally defines relative paths against the process current working directory.
There is no stable authoritative root shared by discovery and downstream normalization.
The failure concerns operating-system file permissions rather than selection of resources for an application-level read-only set.
workflow_graph.entry_state: An existing file is addressable from the authoritative root, but relative pattern discovery depends on ambient current-directory state and can report no match or select a path inconsistent with downstream root-based normalization.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Relative discovery and canonicalization share the authoritative root; from a nested current directory, the intended file enters the read-only set by canonical identity and can subsequently be removed using the same root-relative name, without losing absolute-path support.

steps.condition: Apply when relative pattern expansion currently inherits the process current working directory while downstream path normalization uses an authoritative session root.
steps.validation: Run the nested-working-directory regression oracle: add the root-relative file, compare canonical identity with os.path.samefile, drop it by the same name, and verify absence; also run the existing absolute external-file test.

validation_ladder: Inspect the implementation boundary and confirm relative discovery and downstream canonicalization use the same authoritative root.
Run the focused nested-working-directory test and confirm the canonical file is added to the read-only collection.
Exercise removal with the same root-relative name and confirm the canonical file leaves the collection.
Run the existing absolute external-file read-only test to detect accidental narrowing of accepted path forms.
Run the broader command test suite when its dependencies are available.
Run a patch-integrity check such as git diff --check.
stop_conditions: Stop and defer if the intended base for relative paths cannot be established from command semantics or call sites.
Stop if aligning the base would eliminate required absolute-path support or alter editable-access policy.
Do not claim runtime validation success when the test environment cannot collect the focused test.
unresolved_or_deferred: Focused and broader pytest execution remain deferred because the available Python environments lack required test dependencies.
The GitHub bundle contains no PR discussion, review rationale, or status-check results, so no claims are made about upstream CI execution or reviewer intent.

unresolved_questions: Did upstream CI execute and pass the added regression test? The evidence bundle omits status checks, and local execution was blocked by missing dependencies.
Does the project formally document repository-root-relative semantics for this command? The implementation and test establish that behavior, but no documentation change or PR discussion is available.
